module purpose: neorv32_uart is a bus-accessed UART that stores control settings from bus writes, uses TX and RX FIFOs plus local transmit/receive state to send bytes on uart_txd_o and capture bytes from uart_rxd_i, and generates clock-enable, flow-control, and interrupt outputs.

use-case flows.value: control-register contents: enable, simulation mode, hardware-flow-control enable, clock prescaler, baud divisor, interrupt enables, and RX/TX clear strobes
a transmit request byte accepted into the TX path by writing the data register, allowing the transmitter to leave idle when data is available
TX serialization of buffered data onto uart_txd_o, paced by uart_clk and optional CTS flow control
RX sampling of uart_rxd_i, start-bit detection, deserialization into a byte, and write into the RX FIFO
TX and RX interrupt requests generated from configured threshold bits and FIFO status
RTS flow-control output asserted or deasserted from hardware-flow-control mode and RX FIFO fill level
control/status bits and received RX data returned on bus reads
asynchronous reset clears control, IRQ, engine, overrun, and RTS state; disable, simulation mode, and clear requests clear the FIFOs

conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.enable is written at line 179 and then copied to clkgen_en_o at line 228, used to clear the FIFOs when low at lines 259 and 304, gates IRQ generation at lines 270 and 315, and is copied into the TX and RX engine state at lines 344 and 417. Integrity of this stored setting matters because these flows change between enabled and disabled behavior based on it; availability is also established because the bit is held and exported until rewritten.

ctrl.prsc and ctrl.baud are written at lines 182 and 183. ctrl.prsc selects uart_clk at line 229, and ctrl.baud reloads the transmitter and receiver baud counters at lines 349, 368, 422, and 432. Integrity of these stored values is required for correct serial timing in both TX and RX flows; availability is established because the values are held and reused on every transfer.

ctrl.hwfc_en is written at line 181, reported at line 197, used in the transmitter wait condition at line 359, and selects the RTS behavior at lines 472 to 480. Integrity of this stored mode bit matters because it decides whether external CTS/RTS flow control is obeyed; availability is established because the setting is held until rewritten.

ctrl.clr_rx and ctrl.clr_tx are forced low each cycle at lines 173 and 174 and can be loaded from bus_req_i.data at lines 190 and 191; their asserted values contribute to rx_fifo.clear at line 304 and tx_fifo.clear at line 259. Integrity of these one-cycle stored requests matters because they directly determine when buffered RX or TX data is discarded; availability of buffered data also depends on them.

ctrl.irq_rx_nempty, ctrl.irq_rx_half, ctrl.irq_rx_full, ctrl.irq_tx_empty, and ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf are written at lines 185 to 189 and then used by the interrupt generators at lines 271 to 272 and 316 to 318. Integrity of these stored bits matters because they define which FIFO conditions are allowed to raise IRQ outputs; availability is established because the configuration is held between writes.

The visible local transmit-data store is tx_engine.sreg, loaded from tx_fifo.rdata with a start bit at line 351 and shifted at line 370. tx_engine.txd takes the current serial bit from tx_engine.sreg at line 365, and uart_txd_o copies that value at line 392. Integrity of the outgoing serial frame is established because the transmitted bit stream must follow these load and shift rules; availability is established when data is present and progression conditions at lines 352 and 358 to 377 hold.

uart_rxd_i is sampled into rx_engine.sync at line 408 and shifted at line 410; rx_engine.sreg captures received bits at line 434, and completion at lines 439 to 440 leads to a FIFO write through lines 305 to 306. Integrity of the received byte is established by this sampling and shift sequence, and availability is established when the start edge is detected at lines 424 to 425 and the receive count completes. The readout exit is on transport port bus_rsp_o, so the eligible local references are the input and internal receive-side stores.

rx_engine.over is cleared by reset at line 456 and by disable at line 459, and set when a received-byte write occurs while the RX FIFO is full at line 461; it is reported on readback at line 214. Integrity of this stored status matters because it records the module's implemented lost-data condition; availability is also established because the flag remains set until cleared by the RTL conditions.

irq_tx_o is reset low at line 268 and then updated on each clock by ctrl.enable and the configured TX FIFO conditions at lines 270 to 272. Because this event leaves the entity on irq_tx_o, integrity is established by the exact conditions in those lines; availability is established when those conditions hold.

irq_rx_o is reset low at line 313 and then updated on each clock by ctrl.enable and the configured RX FIFO conditions at lines 315 to 318. Because this event leaves the entity on irq_rx_o, integrity is established by the exact conditions in those lines; availability is established when those conditions hold.

When ctrl.hwfc_en is active, uart_rtsn_o is driven high if ctrl.enable is low or rx_fifo.half is high, otherwise low; when hardware flow control is disabled it is forced low, at lines 472 to 480. This is a decision the module produces for an external consumer, so its integrity is established by those gating conditions; availability is established because the registered output is updated each clock.
